html:
Denmark is a small kingdom between the North Sea and the Baltic, made of the Jutland peninsula and many islands, with Copenhagen as its capital. It is one of the oldest kingdoms in Europe. On the map it appears in the Middle Ages and again from 1815 to now, and in the Americas through Greenland.

The kingdom took shape in the Viking Age. Harald Bluetooth, in the 960s, united the land and made it Christian. His grandson Cnut ruled England, Denmark and Norway together in the early 1000s. In 1397 Queen Margaret joined the three Nordic crowns in the Kalmar Union. After Sweden left it, Denmark ruled Norway for nearly three centuries as Denmark-Norway, until it lost Norway in 1814.

The modern kingdom shrank and turned inward:

  • 1849: a free constitution ended absolute monarchy.
  • 1864: it lost Schleswig and Holstein to Prussia and Austria in a short war.
  • 1917: it sold the Danish West Indies to the United States.
  • 1918 and 1944: Iceland became first a separate kingdom, then a republic.

Germany occupied Denmark from 1940 to 1945. In October 1943 Danes smuggled most of the country's Jews across the water to safety in Sweden. After the war Denmark joined NATO in 1949 and the European Community in 1973. It built one of the world's most generous welfare states, with farm cooperatives and later wind power. Greenland and the Faroe Islands remain part of the realm with home rule.
